subtype: Approach: contact the bank and freeze cards if financial data is affected [Action]
passage:
Sudha: The breach notice says my card number was in it 😰
Noor: Oh no. Did you call the bank?
Sudha: Just did. I used the helpline number written on the back of the card, not the one in the email
Noor: Good call. What did they say?
Sudha: They blocked the card right then, and they're sending a new one. I also asked them to text me for every transaction
Noor: Smart. There are fake helplines out there
Sudha: That's why I didn't search online or use the email. Card first, then I'll change the password on the shop
Noor: Send me a message when the new card arrives 🙂

qa.q: Which number did Sudha use to call the bank?
qa.a: The helpline number written on the back of the card.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling when writing about the card number in the notice?
qa.a: Sudha was worried and alarmed, shown by the worried message, but acted at once instead of freezing.

qa.q: What could Sudha do after the call, and why?
qa.a: Sudha could check the statement for anything unusual and change the shop password, because blocking the card does not fix other details that may have leaked.

qa.q: How might Noor feel about Sudha's quick call?
qa.a: Noor probably feels relieved and a bit proud, having warned about fake helplines and seen Sudha choose the safe route.

grounding: Because a card number was leaked, the person calls the bank on the official printed number, blocks the card and asks for transaction alerts.
